bull.b: High gross and operating margins, together with strong free-cash-flow growth, indicate durable brand pricing power and operating efficiency. These strengths can support reinvestment, shareholder returns, and resilience across the next several quarters.

The upgraded outlook after a strong first quarter signals improving execution and management confidence. Expected revenue growth and further gross and operating margin expansion provide a constructive foundation for sustained earnings progression.

bull.t: Brand Momentum and Global Customer Growth
bull.b: Customer acquisition and strong Asian growth broaden Ralph Lauren’s global demand base. Expanding digital engagement, regional activations, and brand desirability can reinforce customer lifetime value and support continued direct-to-consumer growth.

bear.b: Debt exceeding equity reduces financial flexibility if consumer demand weakens or costs rise. Although profitability and cash generation are solid, elevated leverage can constrain investment choices and increase sensitivity to prolonged operating pressure.

Higher tariffs, freight, labor, and materials costs could weigh on gross margins or require additional pricing. The pressure is potentially persistent over the forecast period, particularly if cost increases outpace productivity and full-price demand.

bear.t: Wholesale Rationalization and Regional Demand Risk
bear.b: Exiting weaker wholesale doors and reducing off-price exposure may improve brand quality over time, but it creates a near-term revenue headwind. Softer European traffic and consumer conditions add execution risk while channels are reshaped.
